title: feat(cli,rest,metadata-protocol): the ceremony carries the sys_metadata organization layer; the anonymous form doors read the environment alone (ADR-0131 D10, C7b S1)
body:
Part of #15211 (stage S1 of C7b; the other stages are this card's S4, #23437, and the split cards #23429 and #23430)
Fixes #23398

Clause-②: no

## What

`os migrate organization-ownership --apply` carries the `sys_metadata` organization layer into the environment, and the anonymous form doors stop reading that layer (ADR-0131 D10; rulings A on #22011 and #22008; ruling 6163114098, Q1 B and Q6 A; seat answer Q2 A).

- **New step `metadata-promotion`, after the authored conversion:**
  - **Form withdrawals are carried first, under every posture, and fail-closed.** When an organization withdrew a public form (`sharing.enabled` or `sharing.allowAnonymous` set to `false`, with the link kept), each view of that name the environment serves still open takes the withdrawal. That covers stored views and views served from code, in every package. The withdrawal is saved through the metadata door, into the view's own package. The judgement is the doors' own predicate (`anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn`), and any organization's withdrawal wins.
  - **Under `single`, an organization customization whose key no other row holds is promoted in place.** This applies to the `view`, `dashboard`, `report`, `translation` and `email_template` rows of `sys_metadata`. The key is (type, name, package, bundle member), and promotion clears the row's `organization_id`.
  - **A key held by more than one row is a conflict.** The plan lists it (`metadataConflicts`, with every row id), and the step blocks on it. The operator chooses one row with `--metadata-choice ROW_ID`, once per conflict. The chosen row is promoted and read back, and any withdrawal an unchosen row holds is carried onto it. Only then are the unchosen rows deleted, by id (Q1 B). No row is deleted before a choice is made.
  - **Under a wall, nothing is promoted unless the operator names the row** (Q6 A). The rest are reported and hold the column.
- **History renumbering (Q2 A), in two steps:**
  - **`version-renumber`, before the promotion.** Where two `(type, name)` lineages exist, the organizations' lineages are laid out one above another and the environment's goes above them all. Each overlay row's `version` moves with its own lineage.
  - **`sequence-renumber`, just before `column-drops`.** Each organization's `event_seq` range moves above the environment's by one offset, and its commit ranges move with it. It runs on every apply, even when checkpointed.
  - **Why it is placed there:** the metadata door numbers a save from history in its own scope. Placed this way, none of the ceremony's own environment saves (the carry, a chosen conflict's carry, the template promotion) can land on a number an organization holds. Order within an organization and the version a rollback resolves are unchanged. Both steps write numbers only.
- **`GET /forms/:slug` and `POST /forms/:slug/submit` no longer read the Default Organization's legacy layer** (#23398). Each candidate is judged against the environment's own view list, which holds one item per package, so a withdrawal in any package closes the name's form in every package. The protocol's undocumented `legacyFormOrganizationId` request key and the merge behind it are deleted. It was never in `GetMetaItemsRequest`, and only those doors passed it.
- The inventory's `environment-overlay-duplicates` category now groups by `bundle_member` too, as the overlay key does.

## Verification (head `b85b0914d`, base `5656c5638a`)

- **cli:** `organization-ownership*` and `commands/migrate`, 36 files, 337 passed, 1 skipped. The typecheck exits 0.
- **rest, metadata-protocol and objectql, re-run on `f5066d7b4`** (these packages are unchanged since `c2d595ee7`):
  - rest `public-form-withdrawal.test.ts`: 27/27.
  - metadata-protocol `protocol.reads-environment-only`, `meta-overlay-cache` and `protocol.org-scoped-write-refused`: 347/347.
  - metadata-protocol `view-container-runtime-expansion`: 203/203.
  - objectql `protocol-org-overlay-registry-gate`: 21/21.
- **Reverse verification.** Each mutation was made with `ablation-replace`, and each restore was verified (blob == HEAD). The first four ran on an earlier head of the same code paths; the last four ran on the final head:

  | Mutation | Pins that went red |
  |---|---|
  | carry removed | 3 |
  | promotion UPDATE removed | 3 |
  | choice fallback removed | the ⭐ "nothing deleted before a choice" pin |
  | the resolved conflict's door save removed | the fail-closed pin |
  | renumber dependents removed | 2 |
  | `sequence-renumber` moved back before the carry | the ⭐ carry pin |
  | the environment lineage laid out first | the ⭐ carry pin |
  | a checkpointed `sequence-renumber` not re-run | the between-runs pin |
- **Narrowed lint** of the 16 changed `.ts` files (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json`): 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`dispatch-gates --ran`:** 76 derived, 76 run, all exit 0, 0 NOT MEASURED. The sweep ran on `f5066d7b4`. Its one red, `check:doc-authoring`, was my own: a tracker number in the inventory's citation string. `b85b0914d` removes it, and that gate then exits 0. That commit changes only that string; the inventory and plan suites (34/34) and lint pass on it.
- **Dogfood** under the verify lock: `showcase-public-form-withdrawal`, `public-form-withdrawal-walled` and `showcase-public-form-withdrawal-layers`, 3 files, 15/15.
- **Dogfood as an operator, on `f5066d7b4`** (`b85b0914d` differs only by that citation string). I booted a real showcase SQLite database once with `objectstack dev --seed-admin`, then stopped it. Into it I planted:
  - an organization-layer withdrawal of `showcase_inquiry.contact` (`allowAnonymous: false`);
  - an environment history lineage and an organization history lineage of that view, each holding `event_seq` and `version` 1–2.

  Then I ran the ceremony with the real `os` binary:
  1. Before it ran, `GET /forms/contact-us` answered 200. The plan run exited 0: 1 promotable row, 0 conflicts.
  2. `--apply` stopped at `rewrite` (see the acceptance notes). By then, `version-renumber` had moved the environment lineage to 3–4. The carry withdrew the package's view through the door and appended the environment's version 5. The promoted row kept version 2, which is still its own snapshot.
  3. I applied the blocker's own remedy in this scratch database (removed the two grants it named) and resumed. `rewrite` and `mirror-deletion` ran, and `sequence-renumber` moved the organization's events to 4–5.
     - Result: no duplicate `event_seq`, and no duplicate `(type, name, version)`.
     - `column-drops` then blocked, because this runtime still declares `sys_metadata.organization_id`. That is S2's schema (#23429).
  4. On a reboot, `GET /forms/contact-us` and `POST /forms/contact-us/submit` answered 404, and no record landed.
  - **This run found a defect, and this PR fixes it.** On `c2d595ee7`, the earlier single step ran before the carry. The carry's door save then landed on `event_seq` 3 and version 3, numbers the step had just given the organization. `f5066d7b4` is the fix, and the ⭐ carry pin reproduces the collision with a door that numbers saves the way the repository does.

## Acceptance notes

- **`Fixes #23398`** per the triage on the card: the organization-layer read the doors kept is gone.
- **The changeset's upgrade example omits `--plan-file`.** That flag is S4's (#23437), which is not on main, and the PRs are not stacked. If S4 lands first, `--apply` also needs `--plan-file plan.json`. S4's changeset states that precondition.
- **The new `steps[].step` values do not widen a released contract.** They are `version-renumber`, `metadata-promotion` and `sequence-renumber`. `--apply` has not shipped in a release (its changeset is still pending). Hence `Clause-②: no` and `patch` changesets.
- **Not S1's.**
  - The dead organization branches in `metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts` and `utils/history-cleanup.ts`, and the remaining engine readers of `organization_id`, belong to S2 (#23429).
  - So does the drop of the `sys_metadata` family's column. Until S2 lands, `column-drops` keeps blocking on those tables, as the dogfood shows.
  - Rows of other types (for example `object` or `flow`) are reported, never promoted (`organization-scoped-other-types`).
- **An observation, not caused by this PR.** On a freshly seeded showcase database, `rewrite` blocks: the grants `--seed-admin` writes (`admin_full_access`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`) name sets the ceremony's catalog does not resolve. It is reported on the card (6163356782).
